_about: Information shown in the Info box of the scenario tool when a celestial body is clicked (display only: the physics uses radar_system.toml [sim.bodies]). Short labels ('labels': the field shown under a short name) and short values (one line each, no wrapping in the Info box); '~' marks an order of magnitude. The last four fields wait for the 2050 lore of TLW (left empty on purpose). Values proposed by the assistant on 29 October 2026, to be checked by the user.

_sources.Earth: NASA Earth Fact Sheet; temperatures: WMO records; dose rates: UNSCEAR 2008 (outdoor, sea level; equivalent dose without radon, ~0.27 uSv/h with it); composition: dry air; perigee / apogee = perihelion / aphelion
_sources.Moon: NASA Moon Fact Sheet; dose rates: Chang'e 4 Lunar Lander Neutrons and Dosimetry, Zhang et al., Science Advances 2020 (absorbed in silicon; 1369 uSv/day); pressure and composition: LADEE, exosphere (collisionless: no volume ratio); axial tilt 1.54 deg to the ecliptic; temperatures: Diviner (polar craters down to ~-248 C)
_sources.Sun: NASA Sun Fact Sheet; IAU 2015 nominal radius; rotation 25.38 d sidereal (Carrington), ~25 d at the equator to ~34 d at the poles; composition by number of atoms (photosphere); orbit around the galactic centre (~26000 ly, galactic year)
